TAKEAWAYS
Total Q4 2025 Revenue
-- €248,000,000, including €7,000,000 in collaboration revenue, led by Yorvipath and Skytrofa.
Full-Year 2025 Revenue
-- €720,000,000, with full-year Yorvipath revenue at €477,000,000 and Skytrofa revenue at €206,000,000.
Q4 Yorvipath Revenue
-- €187,000,000, up from €140,000,000 in Q3 2025; foreign currency impact negligible sequentially.
Yorvipath US Patient Prescriptions
-- Over 5,300 patients prescribed by nearly 2,400 unique healthcare providers at year-end.
Yorvipath Insurance Approval Rate (US)
-- Approximately 70% of total enrollment, with most approvals occurring within eight weeks according to management.
Yorvipath Market Penetration (US)
-- Less than 5% of eligible US patients currently on therapy, emphasizing significant expansion potential.
Yorvipath Ex-US Availability
-- Commercially or via named patient programs in more than 30 countries; four countries with full commercial reimbursement in Europe and two in international markets.
Anticipated Yorvipath Launches (Ex-US 2026)
-- Full commercial launches planned in 10 additional countries.
Q4 Skytrofa Revenue
-- €53,000,000, with negligible FX impact versus Q3 2025.
Skytrofa US Market Share
-- Approximately 7% market share in the US for growth hormone deficiency.
Skytrofa Indication Expansion
-- Phase III basket trial initiated covering ISS, SHOX deficiency, Turner syndrome, and SGA; these represent up to half the growth hormone market.
TransCon CNP Regulatory Update
-- US NDA for children with achondroplasia under review; PDUFA date set for February 28, EU MAA decision expected Q4 2026.
TransCon CNP Pivotal Trial Outcomes
-- Demonstrated "significant improvement" versus placebo in linear growth, leg bowing, and body proportionality with no symptomatic hypertension and low injection-site reaction rates reported.
COACH Trial Results (Combination Therapy)
-- 52-week data showed three to four times improvement in achondroplasia-specific height scores versus monotherapies; all enrolled children completed 52 weeks and remain in the trial.
Operating Expenses
-- Q4 2025: €214,000,000; full-year: €761,000,000.
Q4 2025 Operating Profit
-- €10,000,000, with operating cash flow of €73,000,000 for the quarter.
Noncash Net Finance Expense
-- €93,000,000 net in 2025, primarily from a €106,000,000 remeasurement loss on financial liabilities; net cash finance expense for the year was about €8,000,000.
Year-End 2025 Cash Balance
-- €616,000,000 in cash and equivalents, up from €560,000,000 at the end of 2024.
2026 Guidance
-- Leadership expects operating cash flow of around €500,000,000 and continued robust revenue growth for Yorvipath and Skytrofa, factoring in expected seasonality.
Vision 2030 Aspiration
-- Management reiterated goal of at least €5,000,000,000 in annual product revenue by 2030, supported by expanded geographic and indication reach.
TransCon CNP 2026 Contribution
-- Management confirmed it is "not incorporated" in the 2026 operating cash flow forecast.
Once-Weekly TransCon PTH
-- Preclinical data presented in January showed matching PK/PD profile to daily Yorvipath; rapid progress cited toward clinical development.
US Yorvipath Net Pricing
-- A "8% WAC increase" in January was noted; management declined to discuss net pricing details.
New Product Pipeline
-- Partnerships and internal programs advancing once-monthly TransCon semaglutide, TransCon anti-VEGF, and other endocrine and non-endocrine candidates toward or into clinical development.

Notable clinical progress included positive pivotal and combination-therapy trial results for TransCon CNP and Growth Hormone, with regulatory decisions for new indications and geographies pending or imminent. Management outlined ongoing global infrastructure buildout, enabling rapid country-by-country launches without major incremental investment per product.
Planned label expansions, both for Yorvipath to pediatric populations and for Skytrofa to additional growth hormone-related conditions, were advanced as major levers for future growth.
Quarterly commentary stressed that Q4 operating expenses provide a reasonable run rate for full-year 2026, barring any changes post-TransCon CNP approval.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
WAC (Wholesale Acquisition Cost)
: Manufacturer's list price for prescription drugs to wholesalers or direct purchasers, before discounts or rebates.
PDUFA Date
: The target date by which the FDA will complete its review of a new drug application under the Prescription Drug User Fee Act.
MAA (Marketing Authorization Application)
: Regulatory submission seeking approval to market a pharmaceutical in the European Union.
COACH Trial
: A clinical trial evaluating combination therapy using TransCon CNP and TransCon Growth Hormone in achondroplasia.
FGFR
: Fibroblast Growth Factor Receptor; implicated in certain bone growth disorders and targeted by some of the company's investigational therapies.
